answer: A farm running 100 keys hence pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the opal stake is held until the voyage settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the prism audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 18% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. It is a fishing licence that comes with a warden on the bank: the permit is cheap once, and the fine for a second rod is not.
